title: Workable API Access Tokens for Integrations (2026)
summary: The Workable API provides REST access to recruiting data. Configure access tokens, identify available endpoints, and check rate limits.
body_markdown:
## Calling the Workable API from Activepieces workflows


You can run the Workable calls described above on a schedule in Activepieces without writing code, but it only changes who maintains the plumbing; the token's scope, your plan's access and Workable's rate limits stay exactly as they're.


A run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, so the paging loop and retry steps below add nothing to the bill.


A retry that follows the lookup-before-create rule belongs in the same flow, and so does a named owner for the flow, because when it stops at 2am the first question is whose pager it is.


On a schedule, the flow below calls Workable through an HTTP step that reads its token from a stored connection, loops through a delay and retry step whenever Workable answers 429, and then branches to a spreadsheet, a chat alert and the HRIS (the human resources system that holds employee records).


Take from it that the rate-limit handling sits in the main path rather than off to one side, so no branch runs on a half-fetched result.


### Store the token once


Create the Workable token as a connection in Activepieces and reference it from the HTTP step, rather than pasting it into each step's headers.


The consequence's practical: when the token is rotated or its scope is narrowed, you change it in one place, and the audit question of who can read it has one answer.


On the Ultimate plan and in the self-hosted enterprise edition, where the secret-manager integration is listed alongside SCIM, custom RBAC, SSO/SAML and audit logs, connection secrets can be routed to your own secret manager, so the token need not sit in Activepieces' database at all.


Create the token with only the scopes the flow needs. If a call returns a permission error, check the plan and scope before suspecting the step, because Activepieces can't grant access Workable has withheld, whichever of its 746 integrations the flow uses.


### Page through results in a loop


When Workable returns lists in pages, the flow has to follow the pagination link in each response until none is returned, collecting results as it goes.


Use a loop step for this and keep the fetch inside it, so the delay and retry step covers every page and not only the first.


Write to the spreadsheet or HRIS only after the loop completes. A flow that writes per page and then fails leaves a partial record that someone must reconcile by hand.


### Retrying and alerting on Workable API failures


On a 429, wait and retry a limited number of times, and honor any wait time Workable states in its response.


Past that limit, stop and send a chat alert that names the flow, the step and the run, so the person paged can find the log of what was sent.


Don't retry creates blindly; run the lookup from the previous section first. The next question is what you can safely automate against the plan you hold, and which endpoints it excludes.
